name: Gran Canaria
title: Holidays in Gran Canaria
intro: Golden dunes, year-round sunshine and a Christmas nativity made of sand, about four hours from the UK. Here's what Gran Canaria is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: October to March is the best time for winter sun, at around 20 to 24°C, with Christmas and New Year the busiest and dearest weeks. Summer is hot and busy, with the south sunnier than the north all year.

things.name: Maspalomas Dunes
things.blurb: Huge golden sand dunes running down to the sea, like a small desert.

things.name: Sand nativity at Las Canteras
things.blurb: Each Christmas, sculptors build a big nativity scene from sand on Las Palmas's city beach.

things.name: Puerto de Mogán
things.blurb: A pretty harbour of flower-covered houses and canals, with a calm beach for little ones.

things.name: Palmitos Park
things.blurb: A zoo and botanical park with dolphins, birds of prey and a butterfly house.

things.name: Aqualand Maspalomas
things.blurb: The island's biggest waterpark, with slides for all ages.

things.name: Roque Nublo
things.blurb: A short, steep walk to a giant rock pillar in the mountains, with views to Tenerife's Mount Teide.

faqs.question: Is Gran Canaria good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's warm all year, the flight is about four hours, and there are calm beaches, waterparks and plenty of family hotels.

faqs.question: Is it warm at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Yes, usually 20 to 24°C in the day, warm enough for the beach. Evenings are cooler, so pack a jumper.

faqs.question: Which area is best for families?
faqs.answer: The south, around Maspalomas, Meloneras and Puerto de Mogán, is sunniest and has the calmest beaches.

faqs.question: Gran Canaria or Tenerife?
faqs.answer: Both are warm in winter. Gran Canaria has the dunes and a lively capital. Tenerife has Mount Teide and Siam Park.
